title: Why New Orleans musicians are friendlier
summary: Russell and Hogan discuss why New Orleans musicians seem kinder than New York's commercial ones.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: I don't know. It's something about the city. It's something about the music maybe that makes them better people. There's a friend of mine, Ralph Collins, always had that theory too. He said he wanted to really test it when he got to New Orleans. He figured a good guy is going to be a good musician. The good musicians are good guys and that's, it's almost always that way. They're not perfect either. Everybody has plenty of faults, but I mean they're not small people or crooks or all that. I mean they're, they're nice, nice people.
Most of them, a lot of them have always been very friendly.
So we figure maybe the music does something for them. I don't know.
Well, you think that maybe it has something to do with the general environment.
